trigger: The separately archived 0.1.13 owner run reached three terminal scale streams, then panicked while locating an HTTP header delimiter in the context-rejection response. Its exact backend response and exception were not captured. This review addresses a source-derived reproducible protocol defect without rewriting the original failure classification.

prismReview.typedCapacity: A value-free concrete TokenLimitExceeded marker is produced only for encoded token output or explicit special-token insertion capacity. Its propagation through BPE, Tokenizer, TokenizationSession, SwiftChatSession and SwiftSession preserves the concrete boxed type; display strings never classify protocol failures.
prismReview.otherErrors: Byte/piece safety limits, missing normal byte vocabulary, bad schema, UTF-8 failures and allocation errors retain their existing distinct types. The zero-capacity BPE path checks missing byte vocabulary before reporting capacity overflow, preserving corruption classification. Native Swift only maps the concrete marker to ContextLimit under its already validated context/output reservation.
prismReview.privateResponse: An authenticated private count that fails with ContextLimit emits only fixed 413 JSON with the exact code context_length_exceeded, bounded length, connection-close, no-store and nosniff headers. Other pre-output admission failures keep the generic 400 response. No error response is appended after generation output has started.
prismReview.ownership: Worker Count clears its earlier retained prepared input before preparation. Context rejection performs no generation and does not fault a healthy owner, so a fresh authenticated count/generation can proceed without reset. The old counted input cannot be generated after rejection. Existing post-generation fault/reset, acknowledgement, cancellation and worker ownership rules are unchanged.

runnerReview.routeAndStatus: Only the private input_tokens route admits HTTP 413 as a candidate context rejection. Generation still requires HTTP 200. Every other status remains an unclassified backend failure.
runnerReview.framingAndMetadata: The existing strict bounded HTTP header/body decoder handles the error. The count-error branch additionally requires JSON media metadata, no content encoding and singleton connection-close/no-store/nosniff values; ambiguous framing, duplicate protected fields, trailers and upgrades reject. Body consumption stays within 4096 bytes and the original absolute deadline.
runnerReview.schema: Only the strict nested error object with exactly the string code context_length_exceeded becomes Admission(ContextLimit). Missing, duplicate or unknown fields, wrong types, alternate codes, trailing JSON values and oversized/truncated bodies remain failures. A status alone never supplies classification.
runnerReview.publicOutput: The supervisor uses the existing fixed public 413 admission response and does not connect generation. Private headers, keys and payload details are not forwarded. Unknown failures retain the existing fail-closed disposition.
runnerReview.sharedResponseRefactor: The ordinary metadata validator still checks HTTP 200 before calling the factored content-metadata helper. Only the count-error branch calls that helper after its own explicit 413 status check; no generation success policy is widened.

harnessReview.partialFailure: The pure context receipt helper records response byte count/SHA-256, delimiter observation and fixed payload verdict without publishing arbitrary response text. An unframed or malformed response returns a pending observation rather than unwinding before owned cleanup and final power capture.
harnessReview.framingCorrection: The first draft located one Content-Length and could accept ambiguity. The reviewed followup rejects duplicate Content-Length values, Transfer-Encoding alongside fixed framing, nondecimal lengths and malformed line endings, and tests those adversarial cases.
harnessReview.originalEvidence: This improvement does not recover the unretained bytes, fill the original child's missing powerAfter or make its failed context/Stop/restart workload pass.

reviewedModelFreeRegressionScope: Genuine BPE, special-token and synthetic Swift context overflow retains the concrete marker, while byte/piece/corruption/schema failures remain distinct and the tokenizer stays reusable.
Spoofed error strings and an actual UTF-8 error do not classify as context overflow.
Private worker authentication, fixed 413 versus generic 400, stale-count rejection, no generation and same-owner fresh count/generation without reset are checked using the existing fake engine.
Runner fixed-length/chunked and fragmented count errors, exact strict schema/code, wrong status/media/security fields, duplicate framing, bounds, truncation and deadline expiry are checked.
Supervisor output is fixed and sanitized and never contacts generation after a typed counter rejection.
deliveryBoundary: These source changes require their exact owning hosted checks. Runner's existing 0.1.13 pin and the frozen 90a62b9 trial are not relabelled as having run the fix. A reviewed release containing the Prism change must be delivered and independently qualified before claiming current released-service context recovery or broad PTQ1 promotion.
